subject: Anchored list price, escape clauses, and reseller margin scenarios
messages:
From: Sam Jennings <mike.jennings@clearsky.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Anchored list price, escape clauses, and reseller margin scenarios

Hi Hannah / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profiles and the dedicated capacity options. We've started drafting an RFP and wanted to surface a few commercial questions before we lock timelines with procurement: 

1) Anchored list price + committed consumption: procurement prefers an anchored list price with a straightforward escape clause for usage < X% in Q1. Can you outline how Redwood usually handles escape clauses and whether you allow a reduced minimum in the first quarter without re-pricing the entire PO?

2) Bundled SKUs vs per-token metering: Would Redwood support a hybrid — reserved capacity for the baseline (steady usage) and metered overage? Procurement wants an example pricing cadence for that packaging.

3) Reseller margin & pass-through: We'll likely route purchase via our channel partner (CloudBridge). They require a 12–18% reseller margin, and procurement wants to see examples of how margins are handled in private offer flows (commissioning vs inline discount). Any guidance?

4) Contract artifacts: we attached our current RFP (Clearsky_RFP_v3.pdf). Is there a standard private-offer template you can share that includes the list-price anchor and an escape clause?

Timeline: procurement wants to finalize commercial terms by 09/24 to hit FY Q4 onboarding. Can we set a 30–45 minute call early next week to run through scenarios?

Regards,
Sam Jennings
VP, Cloud Procurement
ClearSky Inc.

Attachments: Clearsky_RFP_v3.pdf (pdf)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jennings <mike.jennings@clearsky.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Anchored list price, escape clauses, and reseller margin scenarios

Thanks Sam — great questions. Looping in Laura from Deal Ops to pull numbers and a brief channel flow. High level answers below so we can hit the call with concrete options: 

1) Anchored list price + escape language: We can do an anchored list price with a 3-month ramp carveout. Typical language we use: if consumption in the first 90 days is < 60% of the committed baseline, the parties agree to a one-time true-up to a pro-rated minimum (not a full reprice). Alternatively, we offer a tiered commit where the first quarter has a 25% lower committed floor to reduce initial risk. We can share both clauses and markups in the PO template.

2) Hybrid packaging: Yes — Redwood supports reserved pools (private/dedicated) for the baseline and metered overage. Pricing examples we propose on calls: baseline reserved @ list price less committed discount, overage at metered per-token rate with a step-down if monthly overage exceeds set thresholds. I'll have Laura drop a sample cadence table.

3) Reseller margin & pass-through: We support two patterns: (a) reseller commission via marketplace pass-through (private offer discount that reduces list price, partner invoice captures margin), or (b) reseller invoiced separately with Redwood net revenue preserved via a commission holdback. For CloudBridge margins in the 12–18% band, we usually map to a 6–10% inline discount + partner commission on top for accounting clarity. Ben, tagging you to confirm the preferred ops path for CloudBridge.

4) Artifacts & timeline: I can share our private-offer template with the anchored clause and a sample pricing cadence table. We can do a ~30 minute call Thursday 09/17 9:00–11:00 PT or Friday 09/18 10:00–12:00 PT. Which works for you?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Anchored list price, escape clauses, and reseller margin scenarios

Hannah / Laura — quick ops POV before the call with Clearsky. I pulled a couple of scenarios into a small matrix (attached: reseller_margin_matrix.xlsx). Key recommendations: 

- Scenario A (Conservative): 10% inline discount to partner + 8% commission via channel invoicing. Best for procurement that wants predictable net revenue and keeps list-price anchor intact.
- Scenario B (Aggressive): 16% inline discount in private offer, partner margin baked into list price. Better if partner insists on margin shown on their invoice, but reduces Redwood's gross list price visibility on marketplace reports.
- Escape clause handling: prefer the "tiered commit" approach (25% lower floor in Q1) to full carveouts — simplifies billing and avoids repeated contract amendments.
- Metering tie-out: set overage step-down bands at 120% / 150% to provide volume discounts on heavy months.

I'll be prepared to share the margin matrix and a sample DocuSign snippet for the anchor language on the call.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Director, Deal Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: reseller_margin_matrix.xlsx

Hannah / Ben / Laura — appreciate the quick turnaround and the matrix.

We reviewed Scenario A & B internally. Procurement is willing to accept the tiered-commit Q1 floor option (25% lower floor in Q1) and prefers Scenario A operationally (10% inline discount + 8% channel commission). Two small asks before we kick off the PO draft: 

- Can Redwood include a one-time true-up calculation example in the PO template so our legal can see the math?
- Please confirm whether partner pass-through will require CloudBridge to be listed on the private offer, or if they can invoice separately (they prefer the latter for downstream reseller accounting).

If that's a yes, please go ahead and send the private-offer template with the anchor clause and the example true-up. Procurement aims to issue a PO week of 09/27. I've attached our PO template for reference.

Sam Jennings
VP, Cloud Procurement
ClearSky Inc.
